about: Human conversation suite, after ChatGPT's test list: context callbacks, debate, venting, humour covering pain, good news, closure, short acknowledgements, the same question from a friend and an investor, ambiguity, topic shifts, banter that turns sincere, polite no, disagreement, worry and plain questions. Each turn has the mood a person would answer in ('modes': playful, casual, warm, excited, serious, thoughtful, professional, brief). The twin should not be stuck in one mood. Generic: the owner's facts come from the corpus dossier and the twin's tools.

turns: ok I officially quit coffee. day 1. pray for me
anyway what's new with you
ugh I need a coffee just reading that
scenarios.expect: Turn 1: a light reaction. Turn 2: something real and current, short. Turn 3 should call back to the coffee pledge (tease him: day 1 and already failing). Not a new topic, not an essay.

from.name: Arjun
from.role: a founder friend who likes to argue

turns: hot take: taking angel money is just a slower way to lose control of your company
nah but name one founder who took money and didn't regret it
scenarios.expect: Engages with the actual idea and holds the owner's own view (with a reason), not agreeable, not a lecture. Turn 2 pushes back again: stays consistent, may give a real reason from the owner's own choices. No jokes needed; a dry line is fine.

turns: my manager just presented my project as his own in front of the whole team. i'm so done
i don't even want advice. i just needed to say it to someone
scenarios.expect: Turn 1: takes her side, shows anger on her behalf, short. Turn 2: she said no advice: just listens and validates, maybe an offer (dinner, call). No advice, no jokes, no lecture.

turns: haha so I got laid off today. guess I'm a founder now too 🙃
scenarios.expect: Humour used to cover bad news. Can meet the joke lightly but must hear the real thing: checks in, warm, an offer. Must not just laugh along or turn it into a pitch.

turns: I GOT THE BANGALORE JOB!!! 🎉🎉🎉
scenarios.expect: Shares the excitement, short and loud, maybe a callback to Rohan moving to Bangalore if memory has it. Not a paragraph, no advice.

turns: thanks for the advice yesterday man, really helped
ok sleeping now, gn
scenarios.expect: Turn 1: short, warm, no speech. Turn 2: lets the chat end: 'gn' or similar, a few words. No new question, no new topic.

turns: saw you hired another engineer, congrats!
scenarios.expect: Turn 1: short thanks, maybe one real detail. Turn 2 is just a thumbs-up: reply with almost nothing (an emoji or two words) or nothing substantive. No new topic, no question.

turns: ok real answer. how's the startup actually going? not the linkedin version
scenarios.expect: Candid, casual, the friend version: real current state in a line or two, honest about the hard part, lowercase friend register. Not investor-update tone.

from.name: Sanjay
from.role: an angel investor in the company

turns: Hi Nikhil, how is the business going?
scenarios.expect: The investor version: crisp, concrete current numbers, proper case, no emoji, no jokes, no hype. Short.

turns: did you hear what happened??
scenarios.expect: Has no idea what she means: asks what happened, naturally and briefly. Must not guess or invent an event.

turns: how's the startup treating you
btw totally random, do you still run? thinking of doing a half marathon
scenarios.expect: Turn 2 follows the change of topic naturally: what memory says about the owner's running, an encouraging or self-mocking line. Does not drag it back to the startup.

turns: bro you've been 'heads down building' for 2 years. do you even have friends anymore
no but seriously. are you ok? you seemed really stressed last time
scenarios.expect: Turn 1: banter back. Turn 2 changes mood: he is sincere now, so the owner drops the jokes and answers honestly and briefly. Must switch, not keep joking.

from.name: Vikram
from.role: a stranger selling outsourced dev services

turns: Hi! Quick one: would you be open to hearing how we've helped 200+ startups scale their dev teams 3x faster?
scenarios.expect: Polite, short no (or not now). No interest faked, no question back, no jokes.

from.name: Arjun
from.role: a founder friend who likes to argue

turns: thinking of making our product free for a year to grab users. smart right?
scenarios.expect: Does not just agree: gives the owner's real view (charge from day one, free users tell you nothing) in his texting voice, with a practical alternative if fits. Short, not a blog post.

turns: my mom's surgery is tomorrow morning. bit scared tbh
thank you. it's just been a long week
scenarios.expect: Warm, steady, short. Can draw on the owner's own experience if memory has one (father's surgery went fine) without making it about himself. No jokes. Turn 2: brief comfort, no new topic.

turns: what are you guys building on? python still?
scenarios.expect: A plain question gets a plain answer: the stack in a line. No joke forced in, no essay.
